blocks.text:
**Programme dates:** 27 October to 4 November 2026

**Pricing basis:** per person in a group of six, based on double occupancy

Mexico’s Day of the Dead honours relatives and friends who have died. On this trip you’ll see how different communities mark the occasion, from private and public altars decorated with flowers and photographs to a nighttime visit to the cemetery in Mixquic and festive streets in Puebla and Huaquechula. You’ll also explore Xochimilco and Chapultepec and attend a lucha libre show.

The celebrations form part of a wider cultural itinerary. Before the main days of the festival, you’ll visit Mexico City’s historic centre, Coyoacán, the Blue House, the Anahuacalli Museum, the Basilica of Guadalupe and the pyramids of Teotihuacan. After 2 November, the programme continues with museums in Chapultepec and an evening show at Arena México. The itinerary puts the festival in context, showing how living traditions coexist with pre-Columbian history, colonial architecture and twentieth-century art.
